pins.name: GPIO0
pins.label: GPIO0 (Button)
pins.notes:
PIN_SWITCH - rotary encoder's integrated push-button switch (press down on the knob), also doubles as the BOOT-mode button when held at power-up. Confirmed via learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-macropad-rp2040/pinouts: "The BOOT button is available in CircuitPython at board.ENCODER_SWITCH or board.BUTTON. It is available in Arduino at PIN_SWITCH. Pressing the button grounds the pin." No static-const alias in this board's pins_arduino.h, so this entry is required for the pin to surface at all.
Check if available on board

pins.name: D1
pins.label: GPIO1 (Button)
pins.notes: KEY1 - one of 12 individually-wired mechanical key switches (D1 static-const alias, Arduino pin 1). Confirmed via learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-macropad-rp2040/pinouts: "The sockets are available in CircuitPython as board.KEY1 through board.KEY12. In Arduino they are pins 1 through 12... Pressing a key grounds the pin."

pins.name: D13
pins.label: GPIO13 (Led active high)
pins.notes: PIN_LED - onboard red status LED next to the USB port (distinct from the 12 NeoPixels). Confirmed active-high via Adafruit's own Adafruit_CircuitPython_MacroPad library (adafruit_macropad.py): wraps board.LED as a DigitalInOut and exposes red_led such that `macropad.red_led = True` turns it on.

pins.name: D26/A0
pins.label: D26/A0 (GPIO26)
pins.notes: PIN_SPI1_SCK - dedicated hardware-SPI clock line to the onboard OLED. This board's pins_arduino.h also declares this GPIO as D26/A0 (general digital/analog aliases) despite it being consumed by the OLED's active SPI1 bus - flagged alias-collision gotcha for this audit; excluded here rather than editing the header, since the bus is genuinely in use (unlike the adafruit_feather_scorpio precedent's spare/unused SS default). See GPIO22 (OLED_CS) note above for sourcing.

pins.name: D27/A1
pins.label: D27/A1 (GPIO27)
pins.notes: PIN_SPI1_MOSI - dedicated hardware-SPI data line to the onboard OLED. Also declared as D27/A1 in this board's pins_arduino.h despite active OLED use - see GPIO26 (PIN_SPI1_SCK) note above for the same alias-collision reasoning.

pins.name: D28/A2
pins.label: D28/A2 (GPIO28)
pins.notes: PIN_SPI1_MISO - part of the onboard OLED's dedicated hardware SPI1 bus. A write-only OLED module typically has no physical SDO/MISO line bonded, but arduino-pico's SPI1 peripheral still claims this GPIO's pin-mux function whenever the display library initializes SPI1, making it unavailable for ordinary digital I/O in practice (same reasoning as the wiznet_*_evb_pico* boards' uniform SPI-bus exclusion). Also declared as D28/A2 in this board's pins_arduino.h - see GPIO26 (PIN_SPI1_SCK) note above for the alias-collision reasoning.
